summary:
Far-right politics in Germany is approaching a milestone. The Alternative for Germany party is leading in Saxony-Anhalt ahead of Sunday's vote, powered by a TikTok-heavy campaign, and a win would put the country's first far-right governor in office since World War II. The result would be watched well beyond the state: it would give the AfD its strongest foothold yet in German politics and test how mainstream parties respond.

Oil markets are feeling the wider war. Prices are up 7.6% for the week, their steepest jump since mid-July, as the US-Iran conflict enters its seventh month. The Strait of Hormuz, which carries about 25% of the world's oil, has been blocked since fighting began, and renewed hostilities have revived supply fears. Separately, Germany has blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport, adding to a string of suspicious incidents across Europe that security services are treating as possible sabotage; Moscow denies involvement.

In Nepal, workers freed two men trapped for nine days in a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower plant, a rare bright spot after floods killed more than 1,250 people and left some 5,000 missing. With many bodies unrecovered, families have begun holding symbolic cremations, including a son lighting a pyre for a straw effigy of his father. In Asia, China and South Korea exchanged formal protests over Taiwan and Korean unity, with Seoul issuing a serious objection and Beijing lodging serious representations — a setback to their recent efforts to improve ties. And in Argentina, President Javier Milei has threatened sanctions as he revives the country's claim to the Falklands, a move critics call politically motivated.

Romanian prosecutors indicted Andrew and Tristan Tate on charges of trafficking minors and money laundering, alleging they recruited victims by seduction and forced them to make pornographic content for a webcam business. Ukraine is pressing airlines to rethink flying to Russian airports as its drone campaign escalates, aiming to close off another part of Russia's airspace. And scientists published research in Science identifying protein interactions linked to profound autism, a finding they call a 'missing piece' in understanding the condition and a possible route to new treatments.

headlines.title: Far-right AfD poised to win Saxony-Anhalt election, raising prospect of first far-right governor
headlines.summary: The Alternative for Germany party leads a TikTok-driven campaign in Saxony-Anhalt ahead of Sunday's vote. A victory would give Germany its first far-right governor since World War II, a political shift with national implications.

headlines.title: Rescuers pull two men alive from Nepal tunnel nine days after flood
headlines.summary: Workers freed two men trapped for nine days in a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower plant. The rescue raises hopes in Nepal, where more than 1,250 people died and some 5,000 remain missing.

headlines.title: Oil prices jump 7.6% as US-Iran war keeps Strait of Hormuz closed
headlines.summary: Oil prices are set for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July, up 7.6%, as the US-Iran war enters its seventh month. The Strait of Hormuz, carrying 25% of world supply, has been blocked since the conflict began.

headlines.title: China and South Korea exchange formal protests over Taiwan, Korean unity
headlines.summary: China and South Korea exchanged formal protests over the Taiwan question and Korean unity, with Seoul issuing a serious objection and Beijing lodging serious representations. The dispute disrupts recent efforts to improve ties.

headlines.title: Argentina's Milei threatens sanctions as he refocuses on Falklands
headlines.summary: President Javier Milei threatened sanctions as Argentina turns back to its Falklands claim. He is seeking to exploit a shifting US stance, but critics say the move is politically motivated.

headlines.title: Romanian prosecutors indict Tate brothers on trafficking minors, laundering charges
headlines.summary: Prosecutors allege Andrew and Tristan Tate recruited victims by seduction and forced them to produce pornographic content for a webcam business. The brothers now face charges of trafficking minors and money laundering; the case moves toward trial.

headlines.title: Ukraine targets Russia's commercial airspace in escalating drone campaign
headlines.summary: Ukraine is pressuring airlines to reconsider flying to Russian airports as drone attacks escalate. Shutting down Russia's commercial airspace would mark a new front in the war and deepen pressure on its aviation sector.

headlines.title: Scientists map protein interactions linked to profound autism, study finds
headlines.summary: Researchers identified key protein interactions that help explain profound autism, a "missing piece" in biological understanding. The findings, published in Science, offer new targets for developing treatments.

headlines.title: Nepal families hold symbolic cremations for flood victims still missing
headlines.summary: With many bodies unrecovered after Nepal's floods, families are performing symbolic cremations, including one son lighting a pyre for a straw effigy of his father. Thousands remain missing across the country.

headlines.title: Germany blames Russia for Leipzig airport attack as Europe investigates sabotage wave
headlines.summary: Germany attributed an attack on Leipzig airport to Russia, adding to a series of suspicious incidents across Europe. Security services are investigating a coordinated sabotage campaign; Russia denies involvement.
